gaps: PML RELOAD OBJECT — command-style PML statement used to reload object definitions from the library. Not explicitly documented in the syntax KB reference (syntax reference covers VAR, IF/ENDIF, DO/ENDDO, DEFINE, etc. but not RELOAD).

Comment prefix --$m — the original uses --$m as a comment line starting with -- followed by $m path reference. KB documents $* for inline comments and -- for full-line comments, but does not mention the --$m convention used in project macros for source-path annotations.

TAGMANAGEMENTTMP custom object — not documented in KB. The object() constructor pattern with a custom type name is KB-confirmed (object LIFE(40) example in Methods on User-Defined Object Types), but TAGMANAGEMENTTMP itself is a project-specific object.

manualValveDescriptionUpdate method — custom method on TAGMANAGEMENTTMP with a query-expression string argument. KB has method call patterns (object.Method(!argument)) but no entry for this specific method.

No error handling — the original macro has no HANDLE/ENDHANDLE block around the object instantiation or method call. If TAGMANAGEMENTTMP fails to load or the method throws, the macro continues silently.
No BADREF/UNSET check after object() — the benchmark reproduces this gap faithfully.

TAGMANAGEMENTTMP is a project-specific PML object (likely defined in a .pmlobj file). No KB coverage for custom object dependencies. The PML RELOAD OBJECT statement implies a dependency on the object being available in the PMLLIB library path.

newEntriesNeeded.title: PML RELOAD OBJECT command
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use PML RELOAD OBJECT to reload a PML object definition from the library before creating instances, ensuring the latest version is loaded.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Place PML RELOAD OBJECT <ObjectName> before object <ObjectName>() in macros that depend on custom object definitions. This is necessary when the object may have been updated in the library without a server restart.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB manual-valve-description.pmlmac
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.manualValveDescriptionUpdate(':RAMTAGOWNER INSET(|RAM|, |AKSO|)')
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern: !tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()  -- may use stale object definition
pitfalls: PML RELOAD OBJECT is a command, not a PML statement — it does not use = assignment.
The object must exist in the PMLLIB library path; otherwise the reload silently succeeds but object() may fail.
In production macros, wrap object() and method calls in HANDLE/ENDHANDLE for safety.
newEntriesNeeded.sourcedoc: AVEVA E3D PML Customization Guide — Macro Programming

newEntriesNeeded.title: Macro error handling pattern — HANDLE/ENDHANDLE around object operations
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Wrap object instantiation and method calls in HANDLE/ENDHANDLE blocks to prevent silent failures.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: After object() construction and before calling methods on custom objects, use: handle any ... endhandle to catch and report errors.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
handle any
  -- error recovery or logging
endhandle
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
PML RELOAD OBJECT TAGMANAGEMENTTMP
handle any
  !tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
  handle any
    !tagMgmt.manualValveDescriptionUpdate(':RAMTAGOWNER INSET(|RAM|, |AKSO|)')
  endhandle
endhandle
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
!tagMgmt = object TAGMANAGEMENTTMP()
!tagMgmt.manualValveDescriptionUpdate(':RAMTAGOWNER INSET(|RAM|, |AKSO|)')  -- no error handling
pitfalls: Nested HANDLE/ENDHANDLE blocks can mask errors from inner blocks if the outer handler catches 'any'.
Using HANDLE ANY on object() may hide library-load issues; consider checking the result before method calls.
newEntriesNeeded.sourcedoc: AVEVA E3D PML Customization Guide — Error Handling
